items.text: the edge of the water as it fills is a soft lens, not a crisp frosted line: a broad smooth swell at the shore that bends the light gently and catches it from a low angle; the darkening of wet ground fades in at the edge; the tremble stays inside the water, slower and gentler

every sequence has an i: a drawer with its version, composer, inspiration and composer notes; write them for your own shows, and they travel with its link and to the room; players open the show's i from the program line

refresh: a show from a link or the room checks for a newer version by the same composer (each version is signed by the composer's device, so nobody else can replace it); a dot says one is out, a tap brings it in and says what changed; if you changed your copy it is kept as "(yours)"
the show is called Current v0.91 (a show you already have under its old name keeps your changes and takes the new name)
share a sequence as a link (Sequence tab › share link): opening it adds the show to anyone's Sequences, ready to play or change
in a room, send to the room: everyone in it gets the show in their Sequences with one tap; send it again after a change and their copy updates
players see the program in the player view: the show's scene now, how many bars are left, and what comes next

the show tells a story: dry air, walking, the first rain on dry ground, the downpour that fills the screen, the shallows, a storm at sea, whales, under water, a quake, surfacing, sun and sky (eleven scenes, about five minutes; Ensemble › Play the show)
six beds for it: Dry air (wind and birds), Walking, Storm, Quake, Surfacing, Sun and sky
a scene can change the level of the bed that is already playing (the light rain, then the downpour)
rain that fills the pool: the water you see falling is the water that fills it (each drop brings what the floor needs to fill on time), and a finger's rain fills where it falls in seconds
shallow water hardly ripples; it trembles with the mixer's sound instead, finer for higher notes, harder for louder
drops on the dry floor are heard (a quiet patter); fewer, larger beads, with a faint lens, read as water rather than glass

the player view's sounds sit in the bar as numbered circles (a filled one plays once, a ring is held, a striped one on the beat; the name on hover): tap plays, hold opens its ring around it, drag the circle onto the pad to place it
record a movement: record in a sound's ring (or a placed sound's halo), drag on the pad, and the sound goes round that path, playing where it is; still stops it

the lower strip holds every control (mix, map, keys, set up, ready, field, level, mute, panic, sound, keys, full screen) and closes; the top only reports; Leave is Place; the regular Sound mixer opens wide in the player view

the player view on a laptop is mostly pad: the upper shelf is the set-up (map, the pad, the key, notes, taps, the field behind, and every sound there is, to add to your part, up to nine); Ready folds it, Set up brings it back

the lower strip is the live part: your sounds as chips (a dot plays once, a ring is held, ticks on the beat), the part's level, mute and panic; tap a chip to play it, hold it for its ring (level, timbre, grain, pitch, what plays it, leave, play, take out), drag it onto the pad to leave it there
